Mary - Album 1: Bloodlines

Where Wolves Wait

"Where Wolves Wait"

[Intro — library cart wheels / books dropping]

Another donation
Another box
Another hundred ways to kill a clock

Accounting
Banking
Taxes due—

Oh wow

Rich people really know how to have fun

[Verse 1]
Came from somewhere up in North Ridge
Past the gates I’ll never see
Private roads and camera towers
Guarding lawns from girls like me

Every corner has a watcher
Every entrance needs a name
Nobody gets through without permission
Guess that’s part of being paid

DELONA FAMILY on the label
Big black letters, perfect print
Boxes full of ledgers, finance
Not a single decent myth

I don’t understand the wealthy
Probably never will, okay
If I ever own twelve houses
Please just take my books away

[Pre-Chorus]
Stack them left
Stack them right
Get this finished before tonight

Banking here
Accounting there—

Then something hits the floor

[Chorus]
Where Wolves Wait
Well, that’s dramatic
Old black cover, cracked and gray

Where Wolves Wait
Okay, you have me
Tell me everything you know today

Fangs and folklore
Moonlit warnings
Ancient curses, silver plates

Everybody else can keep their finance

I wanna know
where wolves wait

[Verse 2]
Must’ve been caught behind the others
Wedged where no one thought to look
Finance leaning into baking—

Honestly, poor little book

Dust along the faded binding
Pages older than the shelf
I pick it up and read the title
Then I nearly lose myself

Werewolves!

Ha!

Now we’re talking

Finally, something worth my shift

I hold it like somebody handed
Me a priceless birthday gift

Finish shelving twice as quickly
Probably broke a personal best
Cart goes back, the floor is quiet—

Now the good part
Now I rest

[Pre-Chorus]
Desk lamp on
Chair pulled near
Come on, wolves
Your scholar’s here

Open page—

…

Oh.

[Chorus]
Where Wolves Wait
I can’t read it
Every sentence laughs at me

Where Wolves Wait
That feels Spanish
Which is deeply inconvenient, see

Fangs and folklore
Moonlit warnings
Probably something fascinating

Of all the languages this book could choose—

Of course it picks
the one I hate translating

[Instrumental break — fast punk guitar / keys underneath]

No.

Absolutely not.

You do not get to beat me
just because you have accents.

[Verse 3]
Spanish-English
English-Spanish
Reference aisle, second row

Found a dictionary thick enough
To break a toe if dropped below

Perfect

Back behind the counter
Old book open, pencil ready

One word here
One phrase there

This might take—

…forever

Great.

[Build]
But I’ve got time
And I’ve got stubborn
And I’ve got absolutely no social life

So really

Who’s winning?

[Pre-Chorus]
Ten grows closer
Streetlights glow
One more page before I go

Library empty
Night outside—

Then the front-door bell rings

[Music drops]

…

This late?

[Final Chorus — half-time into full lift]
Where Wolves Wait
Page still open
Dictionary underneath my hand

Where Wolves Wait
Half-translated
Half a mystery I don’t understand

Old donation
Rich man’s district
Some forgotten family crate

Maybe it’s nothing
Probably nothing

Just another book
That somehow lost its place

[Outro — door hinge / footsteps]

I look up from behind the desk

A man walks in

Too late for browsing
Too calm to hurry

He looks straight at me

And says—

“Hey.”

[CUT]
